In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Zukhruf

It is Meccan.

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ We have already mentioned the meaning of Ha Mim.

The Qur'an is the Clear Book (al-Kitab al-Mubin). As for His saying, ﴿And by the Clear Book﴾, it refers to the Qur'an, and He named it "clear" (mubin) because in it guidance is made clear from error, and good from evil, and in it is made clear everything that is to be done and everything that is to be avoided. The meaning of the verse is an oath: it is as if He swore by Ha Mim and by the Qur'an. The answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾. Likewise His saying: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book with Us﴾ is also the answer to the oath.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have made it﴾. Al-Suddi said: "We have sent it down." Mujahid said: "We have spoken it." It is reported from some of them: "We have made it clear," as Sufyan al-Thawri said.

Those who claim that the Qur'an is created have used this verse as evidence, and they mention that *al-ja'l* (making) here means *al-khalq* (creating), based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who has made the earth for you a cradle﴾, meaning: created it for you. In our view, this argument is invalid. The Qur'an is the uncreated speech of Allah, and the consensus of the People of the Sunnah is upon this. They held that whoever says it is created is a disbeliever, because that involves negating the speech of Allah, the Exalted. We have already explained the meaning of this verse according to the early scholars and those whose exegesis is relied upon.

The word *al-ja'l* occurs in the Qur'an without the meaning of *al-khalq*. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, into females﴾. Its meaning is that they attributed femininity to them, and the meaning is not that they created them.

His saying: ﴿an Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning: in the tongue of the Arabs.

His saying: ﴿so that you may reason﴾, meaning: that you may understand what is in it.

The words of God Most High: ﴿And indeed it is in the Mother of the Book﴾ means: the Qur'an is in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

In some exegeses it is mentioned that the Mother of the Book is with God Most High, in which all things have been made clear. When the Day of Resurrection comes, what was written in the writings is compared with that record, and so they are found to be the same.

It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The first thing God Most High created was the pen. He said to it: 'Write.' It said: 'What shall I write?' He said: 'What will be until the Day of Resurrection.'"

His words: ﴿with Us﴾ mean: with Us.

His words: ﴿Exalted﴾ mean: lofty, such that no one can reach it by alteration or change.

His words: ﴿Wise﴾ mean: its verses are made firm, nothing is added to them and nothing is taken away from them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 5:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Shall We then turn away the reminder from you, out of neglect?﴾ mean: Shall We then overlook you, although you have denied My signs and abandoned My commands? Al-Qutaybi (al-Qutaybi) said: This is taken from their saying: "Fulan struck his mount and turned away from him (ṣafaḥa ʿanhu)," meaning he inclined away from him. The true meaning is: Shall We turn the reminder away from you, turning aside (ṣāfiḥīn), that is, shall We leave you to yourselves, abandon you, so We do not command you, nor forbid you, nor make known to you what is obligatory upon you? ﴿Because you are a people who transgress.﴾ That is, because you are a people who transgress (li-anna kuntum qawman musrifīn). It is also said that the meaning is: We leave you in your denial and do not punish you for it.

The Most High said: ﴿And how many a prophet did We send among the earlier peoples?﴾ *Kam* (كم) is for multiplication, meaning "how many" in the sense of abundance.

And His saying: ﴿among the earlier peoples﴾ means: in the past centuries.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And there did not come to them any prophet except that they used to mock him.﴾ That is, they would ridicule (him). This is said as the most likely interpretation, because some of them did believe.

"And His saying: ﴿So We destroyed those who were stronger than them in might﴾, meaning: So We destroyed those who were stronger than your people in might, i.e., in strength (quwwa).

And His saying: ﴿and the example of the former peoples has passed on﴾, meaning: the punishments of the former peoples. He mentioned it with the word "example" (mathal) in the sense that it is the custom (sunna) of the deniers before them. It was also read as "mithl al-awwalin" with the mim and the tha' vowelled with a damma, in the plural form, and its meaning is what we have explained."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?"﴾ That is: "And if you asked the polytheists, 'Who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth?'" ﴿They will surely say, "They were created by the Almighty, the All-Knowing."﴾ This is said by way of marveling at their condition, that is: How do they worship idols and claim that Allah has a partner, when they have acknowledged that Allah the Exalted is the Creator of the heavens and the earth?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Who has made the earth a cradle for you﴾. This is the beginning of a statement from God, may He be exalted, and is not a quotation of the disbelievers, because their speech was complete in the first verse.

And His saying: ﴿and made for you therein roads﴾ (wa ja'ala lakum al-ard mahdan) — we have already explained it before.

And His saying: ﴿and made for you therein roads﴾ (subulan), i.e., paths [ṭuruqan].

And His saying: ﴿so that you may be guided﴾, i.e., that you may be guided by traversing them in your journeys. It was also said: in your livelihoods and your dealings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 11:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who sends down water from the sky in a measured amount﴾, meaning: in a known measure, so that it is neither less than what people need, so they would not benefit from it, nor more, so that it would become a destructive flood. This is the case in most circumstances, though it may sometimes be otherwise.

His saying: ﴿So We revive thereby a dead land﴾, its meaning: We give life thereby to a dead earth.

His saying: ﴿Thus you will be brought forth﴾, meaning: you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 12:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And He who created all the pairs﴾, meaning: all the kinds. It is said: for every two things that are counterparts, there are two spouses (zawj), and each of them is a spouse of the other. These are: the heaven and the earth, the night and the day, the sun and the moon, Paradise and the Fire, and what is similar to these. Likewise, what pertains to the states of a human being: sickness and health, poverty and wealth, good and evil, sleep and wakefulness, and what is similar to these.

And His words: ﴿And made for you ships and cattle, on which you ride﴾. Al-fulk (ship) is the ships. There is disagreement regarding al-an'am (cattle). Muqatil held that they are camels and cattle. The second view is that they are camels specifically, and this is the more preferable view. Abu Mu'adh al-Nahwi said: "And when did one ride a cow?" In some reports it is related that a man rode a cow, and the cow spoke and said: "We were not created for this; we were created only for plowing."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 13:

And His saying: ﴿So that you may sit firmly upon their backs﴾. If it is said: How is it that He did not say "upon their backs" (ẓuhūrihā), when the plural form has already been mentioned? The answer: His saying ﴿upon their backs﴾ (ẓuhūrihi) refers back to the word "mā" (that which), and its meaning is: so that you may sit firmly upon the backs of that which you ride.

And His saying: ﴿Then you may remember the favour of your Lord when you are firmly seated upon them, and say: Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves (muqrinīn)﴾. That is, muṭīqīn (capable of it); that is, we would not have been able to tame it and subdue it had God Most High not tamed and subjected it for us. ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib said:

(And the tribes know well what ʿAqīl is for us in calamities, as one who is able to subdue them.)

It is related from some of them that he mounted his camel and said: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves." Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, may God be pleased with them both, heard him and said: "Is this how you were commanded? You were only commanded to remember the favour of God Most High and then say this. So when you mount, say: 'All praise is due to God, who guided us to Islam and bestowed upon us Muḥammad, and all praise is due to God, who made us the best community brought forth for mankind,' then say: 'Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us.'"

It is established through the narration of Ibn ʿUmar that the Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he mounted his camel while setting out on a journey, would say "Allahu akbar" three times, then say: "Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves. O God, we ask You on this journey of ours for righteousness, piety, and deeds that are pleasing to You. O God, make this journey easy for us and fold up its distance for us. O God, You are the companion on the journey and the one who watches over the family. O God, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travel, from a grievous sight, and from an evil return in regard to family, property, and children." And when he returned he would say: "We are returning, repentant, worshipping, and praising our Lord." Muslim recorded it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

In some books, it is related from Sulaymān ibn Yasār that he said: "We were on a journey, and whenever people settled upon their mounts they would say: ﴿Glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves﴾. A Bedouin was on a lean camel, and he settled upon it and said: 'As for me, I am able to subdue this.' So it reared with him, and he fell, his neck broke, and he died."

Also in some reports: a young man went out wearing a fine garment, having combed his hair, and it was said to him: "You look handsome today." He said: "Indeed God is pleased with my beauty." So God Most High transformed him.

It is also related from some of them that he used to write the Qur'an, but his ink congealed and no water was available, so he dripped a drop of urine into it and wrote, and his hand became paralysed.
"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, to our Lord we are surely returning﴾ — meaning: returning."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 15:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they have made for Him from His servants a portion﴾, i.e., a share. The share they assigned to God, the Exalted, is that they said: "The angels are the daughters of God, the Exalted." It is said: "ajza'at al-mar'ah" (she bore a female child) when she gave birth to a daughter.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, man is clearly ungrateful﴾, i.e., he is ungrateful for the blessings, manifestly so.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has He taken daughters out of what He creates, and chosen sons for you?﴾ Its meaning: Has Allah taken daughters out of what He creates? ﴿And chosen sons for you﴾, that is, He has selected sons for you. This is in the form of a denunciation of their statement.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is mentioned that this statement was made by the Banu Kinanah and the Banu 'Amir, and a third tribe. It is also reported from some of them that all of Quraysh used to say it. It was said to them: "From where do you say this?" They replied: "We heard our fathers saying so, and we bear witness that they did not lie."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 17:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And when one of them is given the good news of that which he attributes to the Most Merciful as a likeness﴾ — meaning: that which is ascribed to Allah.

And His words: ﴿his face becomes dark, and he is full of suppressed grief﴾ — meaning: sorrowful and distressed. It is also said: filled with grief and anguish.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 18:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Or one who is brought up in ornaments﴾, meaning: one who is reared and grows up (yuraba wa yunbat). And it has been recited: "Aw man yunsha'" (or one who is made to grow up), meaning: yunbat (is made to grow).

And His statement: ﴿in ornaments﴾, meaning: in jewelry. The ḥilya (ornament) is adornment, and the meaning is that she is occupied with her adornment, having no opinion in matters and no control over affairs.

And His statement: ﴿and in dispute is not clear[-speaking]﴾, meaning: in argument she is weak of speech. It is said in the tafsir: a woman has seldom spoken with an argument and been able to deliver her argument, and it is said: a woman has seldom spoken with an argument without saying something that becomes an argument against her. The verse came as a rebuke to them, meaning: you have made my share from My servants like these, and made your share sons.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they have made the angels, who are servants of the Most Merciful, females﴾. Its meaning: they described them (as such). The word "ja'ala" (made, rendered here) is not here in the sense of "created"; it is only in the sense of description and naming, as when one says: "Ja'ala fulan Zaydan a'lam al-nas" (so-and-so made Zayd the most knowledgeable of people), i.e., he described him with it and ruled for him by that. It is also read: "'inda al-Rahman" (with the Most Merciful), which is an expression for nearness and high rank.

And His saying: ﴿Did they witness their creation?﴾ Its meaning: did they attend their creation, so that they knew that they were created as females? It is also read: (ashhadu khalqahum), meaning: attend.

And His saying: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded﴾. It is also read (sanaktub) with the letter nun, meaning: [they] will be recompensed for their false testimony. It has also been said: "sanaktub" is for emphasis.

And His saying: ﴿and they will be questioned﴾, i.e., they will be questioned about their testimony on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 20:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them."﴾ have been used by the Qadariyya (those who affirm human free will and deny divine predestination) as evidence for their doctrine. They said: Allah the Exalted related of the disbelievers that they said, "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them," and then He followed it with denunciation and threat, saying: ﴿They have no knowledge of that. They only guess.﴾ That is, they lie. And you claim that the matter is as they said.

The answer is in two respects. The first: the meaning of His words, ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, is: they have no knowledge for their saying that the angels are daughters of Allah; ﴿they only guess﴾ means: in this statement. The discourse is complete at His words, ﴿If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them,﴾ and the denunciation does not refer back to it. It is also permissible that what is related from the disbelievers be something true, like His words: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Spend of what Allah has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Shall we feed one whom Allah could have fed if He willed?"﴾ and this statement is true and correct. If it is said: the beginning and end of the verse come out as a denunciation of them, so how can something true be related from them? The answer: they said this not out of belief in the truth, but to repel obligation from themselves, since they had been commanded to accept guidance; so they wanted to repel the obligation from themselves by this statement, just as in the other verse they wanted to repel the command to spend by what they said. A statement made with this intention is not valid.

The second: the meaning of His words, ﴿They have no knowledge of that﴾, is: they have no excuse in this statement. And His words, ﴿They only guess﴾, mean: they seek, through this speech, an excuse that does not exist. This was related by al-Nahhas, and the first view was mentioned by al-Farra', al-Zajjaj and others.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Or have We given them a Book before this, so that they hold fast to it?﴾ That is: [an answer to] what they claimed, that the angels are females.

And His words: ﴿so they are holding fast to it?﴾ That is: holding fast to it. This too is in the manner of rebuke and denial.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, they say: "We found our fathers following a community (ummah), and we are guided by their footsteps."﴾ It is also read as "imma" with a kasra on the alif. So his saying ﴿ummah﴾ means: on a religion (millah) and a creed (din). The poet said:

(I swore an oath, leaving no doubt in your soul... Would one who has a religion (ummah) and is obedient commit sin?)

That is, one who has a religion (millah).

As for "imma" with a kasra on the alif, it means the way (tariqah). The poet said:

(Then after success and kingship and imma... their graves gathered them there)

So his saying "wal-imma" means: the good way (al-tariqah al-hasanah).

And his saying ﴿and we are indeed following their footsteps (athar)﴾ means: we are followers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Likewise, We never sent a warner before you to any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ That is: its mutrafun, those who lived in luxury. The point of the disapproval is that comfort prevented them from seeking the truth.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps﴾, its meaning is apparent.

In the two verses there is evidence for the blame of taqlid (blind imitation, following authority without proof) and for returning to the sayings of the forefathers without evidence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 24:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said: "Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers following?"﴾ Its meaning: "Will you follow what you found your fathers upon, even if I bring you something better guided than it?"

And His words: ﴿They said: "Indeed, we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent."﴾ That is: deniers (jahidun).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾, meaning: by destruction and punishment.

And His saying: ﴿So look how was the end of those who denied﴾, meaning: those who rejected (al-jahidun).

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free from what you worship"﴾. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "Bari'" (بَرِيء). So His saying "bara'" (برَاء) has the same meaning as "bari'" (بَرِيء). It is said that it is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, meaning His saying "bara'" (برَاء), and it is one of those words that is neither made dual nor plural.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 27:

As for His saying: ﴿Except He who created me, for He will guide me﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: it is a genuine exception (istithna' muttasil), except that they used to worship Allah and other than Him, so the exception is sound on this view. The second: it is a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "But He who created me" (lakin li-alladhi fatarani), i.e., made me; ﴿for He will guide me﴾, i.e., will give me guidance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 28:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And He made it a word that remains﴾. Mujahid said: It is the statement "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh). Qatadah said: It is sincerity (al-ikhlās) and monotheism (al-tawḥīd). It is related from some of them that the word is the statement of Ibrahim: ﴿I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds﴾. This was when it was said to him: ﴿Submit﴾.

As for His words ﴿in his offspring (ʿaqib)﴾, it means: in his descendants (walad). In the exegesis: there will never cease to be, among the descendants of Ibrahim, one who remains upright upon the word of monotheism. It was also said: ﴿in his offspring﴾ refers to one single man, and that is Muhammad (ﷺ). Al-Suddi said: "in his offspring" means: among the family of Muhammad, may Allah be pleased with them.

As for His words ﴿so that they may return﴾, it means: that they may return to guidance after misguidance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Nay, I gave these people and their fathers enjoyment﴾, meaning: I gave them enjoyment through their own selves, their wealth and their children, and I gave enjoyment to their fathers.

And His saying: ﴿until there came to them the truth and a clear messenger﴾, meaning: there came to them the Qur'an, making clear the guidance from error, and the truth from falsehood.
And His saying: ﴿When the truth came to them, they said, "This is magic, and we are disbelievers in it."﴾ That is: deniers.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And they say: "Why was this Qur'an not sent down upon a great man from the two towns?"﴾ Its meaning is: upon a great man from one of the two towns. The two towns are Makkah and al-Ta'if. As for the two men, the commentators differed about them. Ibn 'Abbas said: the one from Makkah is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and the one from al-Ta'if is Habib ibn 'Amr al-Thaqafi. It was also said: the one from Makkah is 'Utba ibn Rabi'a, and the one from al-Ta'if is 'Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi; this was related by Qatada. Mujahid said regarding the one from al-Ta'if: he is Ibn 'Abd Yalil al-Thaqafi. And it is also related from al-Suddi regarding him that he was Kinana ibn 'Adi ibn 'Amr.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 32:

And His saying: ﴿Do they apportion the mercy of your Lord?﴾ That is: the message of your Lord, so that they choose for it whomever they wish. Its meaning is that they have no such choosing.

And His saying: ﴿It is We who apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾ That is: just as We apportioned the livelihood of this worldly life, choosing for wealth whom We wish and for poverty whom We wish, so likewise We chose and selected for the message whom We wish. It has been related from Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has apportioned your characters among you just as He has apportioned your provisions among you. Allah gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He does not love, but He gives religion only to whom He loves. Whoever He gives religion to, He has indeed loved him." And from Qatadah: "How many a weak man (in constitution), inarticulate of tongue, has been granted expansion in provision, and how many a strong man (in constitution), eloquent of tongue, has been restricted in provision."

And His saying: ﴿And We have raised some of them above others in degrees﴾ That is: in this world, so one is rich and another poor, one is superior and another inferior, one is free and another a slave, one is healthy and another sick, and similar things.

And His saying: ﴿so that some of them may take others in service⁠

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Were it not that mankind would become one community﴾, its meaning: Were it not that all of mankind would be disbelievers. It was also said: Were it not that the world would incline people away from the religion, we would have done this to the disbelievers, because of the lowliness of the world in Our sight.

And His saying: ﴿We would have given to those who disbelieve in the All-Merciful, for their houses, roofs of silver﴾. It was read "saqfan" (roofs) with a fatha on the sin, meaning: We would have made their walls of silver.

And His saying: ﴿And staircases of silver upon which they would ascend﴾, that is: We would have made for them ladders of silver upon which they would climb onto the roof. Its meaning: yazharun (they would ascend), they would go up and rise high.

In the reports it is related that Nabigha ibn Ja'da recited to the Prophet (ﷺ):

(He has reached the heaven in chastity and generosity... and indeed we hope for a higher manifestation beyond that.)

That is, a height (mu'allan). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Where to, O Abu Layla?" He said: "To Paradise." He said: "Indeed, if Allah wills."
And His saying: ﴿And for their houses, doors and couches (sururan) upon which they recline﴾ — meaning: We made that for them of silver.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 35:

And His saying: ﴿And ornaments of gold﴾ has two opinions. The first: "and gold," meaning: (We made) all of that from gold. If someone asks, "Why is it in the accusative (naṣb)?" we say: because the meaning is "from silver and from gold," so the preposition "min" (from) was removed and the word became accusative. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is "wa-dhahaban" (and gold), and this clarifies the correctness of this opinion.

The second opinion: His saying ﴿and ornaments﴾ means: wealth (ghina). It is reported from al-Hasan that he said: "Al-zukhruf (ornaments) are the engravings (naqsh)." It was also said: "Everything that is adornment in this world."

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, all that is but the enjoyment of the life of this world﴾ means: it lasts for a period and then passes away quickly.

And His saying: ﴿And the Hereafter with your Lord is for the righteous﴾ means: for those who are righteous (al-muttaqun) from shirk and sins.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 36:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾. Qatada said: "He turns away." From this comes the saying of people: "So-and-so ya'shu," meaning he walks with weak sight. It is said: "ʿashā yaʿshū" when his sight weakens, and "ʿashā yaʿshā" when his sight is blinded, and from this comes al-Aʿshā (the one with weak sight). In a hadith it is related that Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab lost one of his eyes and began to ya'shu with the other, meaning he saw with weak sight. It was also recited as "yaʿsh" with a fatha on the shin, meaning he is blinded. It is said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful﴾, that is, he goes away from His remembrance, so he proceeds in darkness and stumbling, out of ignorance.

And His words: ﴿We appoint for him a devil﴾, meaning, We assign to him a devil. It is said: "We cast him with a devil." And in the tafsir it is related that when the disbeliever comes out of the grave, a devil meets him, places his hand in his hand, and does not leave him until he arrives at the Fire. As for the believer, when he comes out of his grave, an angel meets him, places his hand in his hand, and does not leave him until he arrives at Paradise.

And His words: ﴿so he is a companion to him﴾, meaning, one who accompanies him. It is said: they are placed in one chain.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they (the devils) turn them away from the path﴾, meaning: the devils turn them away from the path of truth.

And His words: ﴿and they think that they are guided﴾, meaning: the disbelievers think that they are guided by the guidance of the devils.

In some of the chains of narration (musnad), by way of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Hold fast to La ilaha illa Allah and seeking forgiveness (istighfar), so increase in them, for Iblis said: 'I destroyed the children of Adam with sins, and they destroyed me with La ilaha illa Allah and istighfar. So when I saw that, I destroyed them with desires.'" Then the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: ﴿and they think that they are guided﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 43, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when he comes to Us﴾. It is also read "jā'ānā" (came to us both). So his saying "jā'anā" (came to Us) refers to the disbeliever alone, and his saying "jā'ānā" (came to us both) refers to the disbeliever and his companion, the Shaytan.

His saying: ﴿He will say, "Would that between me and you were the distance of the two easts! Wretched is the companion."﴾ Regarding this there are two opinions. The first: "the distance of the two easts" means the distance between the east and the west. He called them "two easts" according to the custom of the Arabs, for they mention two different things and call them by one name. The poet said:

(We have taken, over you, the horizons of the sky, for us are its two moons and the rising stars.)

Meaning the sun and the moon.

Another said:

(The Basra of the Azd is ours, and Iraq, and the two Mosuls, and from us are Egypt and the Haram.)

By "the two Mosuls" he meant Mosul and al-Jazirah.

It is related that the people of Basra said to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, when they fought him alongside ʿĀ'isha on the Day of the Camel: "We ask you to follow the example of the two ʿUmars," meaning Abu Bakr and ʿUmar. Jarir said:

(The Messenger of Allah would not have been pleased with their deed, and the two ʿUmars, Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, would not have been either.)

The second opinion: "the two easts" means the east of winter and the east of summer.

His saying: ﴿Wretched is the companion﴾, meaning: wretched is the one who accompanies you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged yourselves, that you are sharing in the punishment.﴾ That is: your being punished will not be made easier for you by seeing others sharing in the punishment with you. So it is as if Allah, exalted is He, denied them the consolation (ta'assi) by which a person finds affliction and punishment easier to bear, for when a person is in an affliction and sees another in the same situation, it becomes easier for him. Ta'assi means consolation (tasalli). al-Khansa' said about her brother Sakhr:

(Were it not for the great number of those weeping around me over their brothers, I would have killed myself.)

(They do not weep the way they would for my brother, but I console myself (u'azzi al-nafs [anhu]) through consolation (bi-l-ta'assi).)
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Can you then make the deaf hear, or guide the blind, and those who are in manifest error?﴾ That is: you cannot make them hear, nor can you guide them.

"And as for His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Then whether We take you away, indeed We will take vengeance upon them﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: its meaning is: 'Then indeed We will bring you out of Makkah, and indeed We will take vengeance upon them on the Day of Badr, by killing and capturing.'

The second opinion: ﴿Whether We take you away﴾ means: by death, indeed We will take vengeance upon them after you. It is also said: (the vengeance is) on the Day of Resurrection."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 42:

His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Or We shall show you that which We have promised them﴾. Al-Suddi said: "This refers to the polytheists." Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "This refers to his community (ummah)."

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) was shown some of what his community would come to, and after that he was never seen laughing or cheerful until he passed away from the world.

In some tafsirs: there is no prophet except that he was shown the chastisement (al-niqmah) upon his community, except our Prophet (ﷺ), for Allah, Exalted is He, did not show him the chastisement upon his community. Yet chastisements did befall his community, and they will continue until the Hour is established.

His words: ﴿So indeed, We are over them omnipotent﴾, meaning: able (qadirun).

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So hold fast to what has been revealed to you﴾, meaning: to the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are upon a straight path﴾, meaning: a clear way.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 44:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is an honour for you and for your people.

And His saying: ﴿And you will be questioned﴾, meaning: you will be questioned about the thanks owed for this blessing. And it is reported from Qatadah, or someone else, regarding this verse, that he said: A man is asked, "From whom are you?" and he says, "From the Arabs." Then it is said to him, "From which of the Arabs?" and he says, "From Quraysh." This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾. Some narrators reported from Malik ibn Anas that he said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and for your people﴾ is the saying of the speaker: "My father related to me from my grandfather." But the well-known view is the first one. The meaning of the honour of Quraysh is that the Qur'an was revealed in their language, and the Messenger was from among them.

[And ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers:] Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped? (Q. 43:45)

The commonly known view regarding this verse is that its meaning is: "Ask the nations to whom We sent messengers before you." Ibn al-Anbari said its meaning is: "Ask the followers of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers." Some others said: "Ask those who recite the Book, from among those to whom We sent messengers before you."

In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Ask those to whom We sent messengers before you: Did We appoint gods other than the Most Merciful to be worshipped?" This is an explanation of the well-known reading.

The second view regarding the verse is what 'Ata' narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that God, exalted is He, gathered the messengers on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey) in the mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). Then Jibril called the adhan, then called the iqamah, then said to the Prophet: "Go forward and lead them in prayer." When he finished his prayer, He said to him: "Ask those whom We sent before you of Our messengers." Some claimed that he asked them and they answered, saying: "God, exalted is He, only commanded us with monotheism and sincerity."

In some tafsirs: Mika'il said to Jibril: "Did Muhammad ask the messengers about what he was commanded?" He said: "No, he was more certain and more knowing of God than to ask about that."

If someone says: What is the purpose of the question and answer in this matter? Asking about this would only occur from one who doubts the matter; as for one who is certain, not so. The answer: the purpose of the verse is to affirm the Messenger in what he believes, to rebuke the disbelievers, and to make them acknowledge that the matter is as the Messenger says.

Some others said: The address is to the Messenger, but what is meant is the community. It is also said: the address is to the polytheists, as if He commanded them to ask the believing People of the Book whether God commanded what they claim is in one of their books, namely the worship and veneration of idols. They used to refer to the statements of the People of the Book on some matters and rely upon them. And God knows best.
The word of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and he said, "Indeed, I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds."﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

And His words: ﴿When he brought them Our signs﴾, that is: the miracles and clear proofs.

And His words: ﴿they laughed at them﴾, meaning: the laughter of the mockers and deniers. The purpose of the verse is to express the Messenger's astonishment at their laughter and their denial, despite the arrival of the manifest signs with Moses, may the blessings of God be upon him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 48:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did not show them any sign but that it was greater than its sister﴾, meaning: greater than the sign that preceded it. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash it is related that the first of Musa's signs was that Fir'awn had placed on his palace seven walls, between every two walls a moat and thickets, and the doors upon the walls were locked and could not be opened except by his permission. When Musa arrived at the gate of Fir'awn, the doors opened for him, the locks broke, and the beasts of prey prostrated to him until he reached the palace of Fir'awn. This was the first sign. Then, when Fir'awn brought the sorcerers and they cast their staffs and ropes, which in the eyes of the people appeared like great serpents, Musa then cast the staff that was with him, and it swallowed all the ropes and staffs, as is well known in the story. This sign is greater than the first. Some of them claimed that all the signs are equal in their miraculousness and their indication, except that he called the sign present greater than the one that had passed, because of the presence of this sign and the passing of that one. This is like a man who says about an illness that afflicts him: "No illness has passed over me like this illness," although illnesses greater than it, or like it, have passed over him; but he says this saying because of the presence of this illness and the passing of that illness. Among them is one who said: what is meant by the signs is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood﴾, and there is no sign that manifested after another except that it was greater than the first. What we have mentioned as the first opinion is the best in meaning.

And His saying: ﴿And We seized them with punishment that perhaps they would return﴾, meaning: to Allah, may He be exalted.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 43, verse 49:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And they said, "O you who have been enchanting us, call upon your Lord for us by what He has promised you. Indeed, we are [truly] guided."﴾

If it is said: How did they say, "O you sorcerer" (yā ayyuhā al-sāḥir), and then say, "Indeed, we are guided [through you]" [while no one is guided by a sorcerer]? The answer: the sāḥir (sorcerer) in their view was the ʿālim (learned man, one who knows). The meaning of His words ﴿O you sorcerer﴾ is "O you learned one." This is the view of al-Kalbī and others. Al-Zajjāj said: they said "O you sorcerer" in accordance with what they (used to) say to him. Some of them said: they only said this in the manner of mockery and derision, and they had not believed that they would have faith in him.

As for His words ﴿by what He has promised you﴾: they said this because Mūsā (Moses) had told them, "If you believe, Allah will remove this punishment from you." This is mentioned in Surat al-Aʿrāf, as has already been explained.
His words, exalted is He: ﴿But when We removed the punishment from them, behold, they broke their word.﴾ That is, they break the covenant, and they do not keep to what they say.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 51:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Pharaoh proclaimed among his people, saying, "O my people, does not the kingdom of Egypt belong to me?"﴾ Some of them said: his kingdom was forty farsakh by forty farsakh. And some of them said: a journey of forty days by forty days.

And His saying: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾, that is, beneath my palace. Qatadah said: "before me." In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: there were five rivers in Egypt at the time of Pharaoh, which later vanished, and none of them remains. In this same tafsir also: there were seven khalij (canals) in Egypt, the singular of which is khalij, which later vanished, and Pharaoh would ride from Fayyum to Damietta and Alexandria, and he would not travel except beneath dense trees and flowing rivers.

It has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "On the night of the Mi'raj I saw the Lote-Tree of the Utmost Boundary (sidrat al-muntaha), and from its root there issued four rivers: two inner rivers and two outer rivers." He said: "I asked Jibril about the rivers, and he said: As for the two inner ones, they are in Paradise; and as for the two outer ones, they are the Nile and the Euphrates."

And from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As that he said: "Indeed Allah, Exalted is He, nourishes the Nile with all the rivers between the east and the west, and that is at the time of its rising, until the rising reaches its limit, then it returns to what it was."

And His saying: ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ meaning: will you not see? In some tafsirs: the meaning of "rivers" in this verse is wealth, and He called it rivers because of its abundance and its manifestness.

And His saying: ﴿flow beneath me﴾, that is: I divide it among whom I wish. They said: the manifestation of encouragement and power in this is greater than in the rivers; this was mentioned by al-Mawardi Abu al-Hasan al-Qadi.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 52:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Am ana khayrun min hadha alladhi huwa maheen﴾ (﴿Or am I better than this one who is contemptible﴾). Some of them said: His words ﴿am﴾ (or) are connected to what precedes them, and its meaning is: ﴿Will you not see, or do you see?﴾ It was also said: ﴿Or are you not seeing?﴾ and the speech is complete on this reading, then the beginning of His words ﴿ana khayr﴾ (I am better) begins anew. This is related from al-Khalil and Sibawayh. Others among them said: ﴿am﴾ is an extra, redundant particle (sila za'ida), and the discussion concerns His words ﴿ana khayrun min hadha alladhi huwa maheen﴾. In some readings it is recited as ﴿ana khayr﴾ with the emphatic (tafkhim) pronunciation.

His words ﴿min hadha alladhi huwa maheen﴾ mean: weak and despised.

His words ﴿wa la yakadu yubeen﴾ (and he can hardly speak clearly). The people of tafsir said: He only said this because of the speech impediment (lathgha) that was in his tongue, which remained from the knot (uqda) in his tongue caused by placing the ember in his mouth. Others among them said: In his tongue there was something that did not allow him to make his speech fully clear. In support of what we have mentioned concerning His words ﴿am﴾, they cited the verse of the poet:

(O gazelle of the battlefield, between the anklets and between the sand-dune, are you or Salim?)

Its meaning: Are you more beautiful, or is Salim?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 53:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why then have bracelets of gold not been cast upon him?﴾ In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "asawir min dhahab" (bracelets of gold). In the narration about this: they used to, when they adorned [a man] with a bracelet, adorn him with a bracelet of gold on his hand, and place a collar of gold around his neck. The meaning of the verse is that they said: "If Musa were a prophet, why would God not have adorned him with a bracelet, or placed a collar upon him, or sent angels with him as helpers in his affair?" This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿or the angels came with him in procession﴾, that is, following one another in succession.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 54:

And His saying: ﴿So he made his people feel foolish, and they obeyed him﴾. That is: he stirred them, by his calling them to his falsehood, so they became light-minded with him and answered him. It is also said: he incited them (istafazzahum), and they obeyed him out of their ignorance.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were a people who were defiant transgressors﴾. That is: they were going out of obedience. It is also said: "He made his people feel foolish" means he drove them to the lightness of ignorance, for with reason goes dignity (waqar), and with ignorance goes lightness (khiffah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 43, verses 55–56:

The words of the Most High: ﴿When they angered Us﴾. That is: they provoked Our anger and displeasure. If it is said: anger (asaf) only arises over something lost, and God Most High does not lose anything?

The answer to this: its meaning is anger, as we have explained. Some of them said: "they angered Us" means: they did an act which, if they had done it with a created being, he would have been grieved and sorrowful. In some reports: 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr was sitting with Wahb ibn Munabbih when a people came and complained about their governor, and the governor was present. Wahb ibn Munabbih became angry, took a staff and split the governor's head. 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr laughed and said: "Look at this one, forbidding anger and yet getting angry?" Wahb said: "No, do not blame me, for God Most High gets angry, and He is the Creator of forbearance," then he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿When they angered Us, We took vengeance upon them﴾. The meaning of His words ﴿We took vengeance upon them﴾ is: by drowning and destruction, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We drowned them all, and made them a precedent and an example for those who came after﴾, that is: a precedent for the great ones and those after them, and an example for whoever does the like of their deeds. The meaning of "an example" (mathalan) is: a lesson and a warning. It is read "salafan," which is the plural of salif, and it is read "salafan" (a precedent), and the meaning in all of them is one. It is related from Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: "There is no one except that he has a precedent in good and evil."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 43, verses 55–56:

The words of the Most High: ﴿When they angered Us﴾. That is: they provoked Our anger and displeasure. If it is said: anger (asaf) only arises over something lost, and God Most High does not lose anything?

The answer to this: its meaning is anger, as we have explained. Some of them said: "they angered Us" means: they did an act which, if they had done it with a created being, he would have been grieved and sorrowful. In some reports: 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr was sitting with Wahb ibn Munabbih when a people came and complained about their governor, and the governor was present. Wahb ibn Munabbih became angry, took a staff and split the governor's head. 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr laughed and said: "Look at this one, forbidding anger and yet getting angry?" Wahb said: "No, do not blame me, for God Most High gets angry, and He is the Creator of forbearance," then he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿When they angered Us, We took vengeance upon them﴾. The meaning of His words ﴿We took vengeance upon them﴾ is: by drowning and destruction, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿So We drowned them all, and made them a precedent and an example for those who came after﴾, that is: a precedent for the great ones and those after them, and an example for whoever does the like of their deeds. The meaning of "an example" (mathalan) is: a lesson and a warning. It is read "salafan," which is the plural of salif, and it is read "salafan" (a precedent), and the meaning in all of them is one. It is related from Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: "There is no one except that he has a precedent in good and evil."

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And when the son of Mary is presented as an example﴾. Most of the commentators hold that this verse was revealed concerning the dispute of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zabaʿrā with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell﴾. When the words of Allah the Exalted were revealed, ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship﴾, up to His words, ﴿you will be its entrants﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited them to the disbelievers of Quraysh, ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zabaʿrā said: "Is this for us and our gods specifically, or for us and all the nations and their gods?" He said: "Rather, it is for you and your gods and for all the nations and their gods." Ibn al-Zabaʿrā said: "I have defeated you, by the Lord of the Kaʿbah!" Then he mentioned what we have cited earlier concerning ʿIsā, ʿUzayr and the angels, peace be upon them. According to this, the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And when the son of Mary is presented as an example﴾, mean: when they made the son of Mary an example for their gods, and they said: "If the son of Mary is in the Fire, then we are content that we and our gods be in the Fire."

As for His words, ﴿And when your people turn away from it, they clamour﴾, with a kasra on the ṣād, meaning: they cry out in the manner of disputants. It is also said: "yaṣuddūn" means they laugh and rejoice at the words of Ibn al-Zabaʿrā. It has also been read with a ḍammah on the ṣād, and its meaning is: they turn away. There is another view concerning the verse: when the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned the account of [ʿĪsā] to Quraysh, and that Allah the Exalted created him without a father, just as He created Ādam without a father, and mentioned the signs that Allah manifested at his hands, Quraysh began to laugh and said: "What Muḥammad wants from mentioning ʿĪsā is only that we worship him, just as the Christians worshipped ʿĪsā." This is the view of Mujāhid.

"And they say: Are our gods better, or is he?" On the first view, its meaning is: Are our gods better, or is Jesus? Rather, Jesus is better than our gods; so if Jesus is in the Fire, then let our gods be in the Fire. On the second view: Are our gods better, or is he? That is, Muhammad; so if Muhammad is asking us to worship him, then we worship our gods. And in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Are our gods better, or is this one?" and this supports the second view.

As for His saying: "They have not struck it for you except as a dispute" (﴿مَا ضربوه لَك إِلَّا جدلا﴾), it means: they did not say this statement except as argument by means of falsehood; for they knew that the son of Mary does not enter the Fire, and they knew that he was not included in the verse, because God, exalted is He, said: "Indeed, you and what you worship" (﴿إِنَّكُم وَمَا تَعْبدُونَ﴾), and "má" (ما) is for those who do not reason, not for those who reason.

As for His saying: "Rather, they are a people given to dispute" (﴿بل هم قوم خصمون﴾), that is: they are contentious without truth. It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ), by the narration of Abu Umamah (رضي الله عنه), that he (ﷺ) said: "No people went astray after being guided, while they were upon it, except that they were given to disputation," then he recited His saying, exalted is He: "They have not struck it for you except as a dispute. Rather, they are a people given to dispute." The meaning of the verse is disputation by means of falsehood, not disputation in seeking the truth or in clarifying it; for He, exalted is He, has said in another place: "And argue with them in the best manner" (﴿وجادلهم بِالَّتِي هِيَ أحسن﴾), and He, exalted is He, said: "And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner" (﴿وَلَا تجادلوا أهل الْكتاب إِلَّا بِالَّتِي هِيَ أحسن﴾).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 59:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He was but a servant﴾, meaning: Jesus, peace be upon him, and ﴿Jesus, son of Mary, was only a servant﴾, ﴿upon whom We bestowed favour﴾, that is, with prophethood and the signs.

And His words: ﴿and We made him an example﴾, that is, a lesson and a warning for the Children of Israel. It is also said: "We made him an example for them," that is, a human being like them.

And His saying: ﴿And if We willed, We would have made from among you﴾, meaning: in place of you, ﴿angels upon the earth succeeding one another﴾, meaning: they would succeed you. It is also said: some of you would succeed others.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 61:

The Almighty's words: ﴿And indeed, it is a sign for the Hour﴾. Its meaning: that ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) is one of the signs of the Hour, so by his descent one knows the knowledge of the Hour. It is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The son of Maryam will surely descend as a just ruler (ḥakaman muqsiṭan), he will break the cross and kill the pig," and the report continues.

In some reports: that he "will descend at a white minaret (thaniyya) above a mountain of the mountains of Bayt al-Maqdis, upon which are two yellow garments (mumaṣṣaratān), and in his hand is a spear with which he will kill the Dajjal." Ibn ʿAbbās recited: ﴿And indeed, it is a sign for the Hour﴾, meaning: a sign of its approach.

Al-Farazdaq said, praising ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn:

(This is the one whose footprint the Baṭḥāʾ knows, and the Corner (of the Kaʿba) knows him, and the sacred and the unsacred precincts.)

(This is the son of the best of God's servants, all of them; this is the pious, the pure, the chaste, the learned.)

And His words: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path﴾, meaning: do not doubt about it, that is, the Resurrection. The rest is clear in meaning.

Almighty Allah says: ﴿And let not Satan hinder you; indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: Among his enmity is that he expelled your father from Paradise and stripped them of their garment of light.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 63:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said, "I have certainly come to you with wisdom, and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ."﴾ Abu 'Ubayda said: "(The word 'some', ba'd, here means) all of that about which you differ." Another of the linguists said: "'Some' (ba'd) does not validly mean 'all' (kull). The meaning of the verse is: 'and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ concerning the Gospel, and some of that about which you differ concerning other than the Gospel.'" It is also said that its meaning is: "and to make clear to you that about which you have differed in the matter of your religion, not in the matter of your worldly affairs; so it is some of what you have differed about. And Allah knows best."

As for His words: ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾ its meaning is clear.
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ We have already explained it.

Divine statement: ﴿Then the factions differed among themselves﴾. These are the ones who disagreed about Jesus after he was raised up to heaven. Some of them said: "He is the son of God," some said: "He is God," and some said: "He is the third of three."

And His statement: ﴿So woe to those who did wrong, from the punishment of a painful day﴾ — meaning: painful (muji', causing pain).

Almost all of the Qur'anic quotation is in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translating:

The Most High said: ﴿Do they only await the Hour, that it come upon them suddenly (baghtah)?﴾ That is, unexpectedly (faj'ah). And His saying: ﴿while they do not perceive﴾ means they do not know of its coming. The people of knowledge (ahl al-'ilm) said: Allah, exalted is He, concealed the matter of the Hour and the time of its establishment so that the warning and the instilling of fear would be more forceful.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 67:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿On that Day, friends will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾. In the tafsir (interpretation of the Qur'an), it is said that they are Umayyah ibn Khalaf, 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Hafs ibn al-Mughirah, and 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah.

al-Naqqash mentioned that 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt was a friend of Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and that 'Uqbah used to come to the Prophet (ﷺ), sit with him, and listen to his words. Umayyah ibn Khalaf said to him: "You have gone over (to his religion), O 'Uqbah." He replied: "By Allah, I have not gone over." Umayyah said: "My face is forbidden to look upon your face unless you spit in the face of Muhammad." So 'Uqbah did that. The Messenger (ﷺ) said to him: "If I ever get you outside the Sacred Precinct (Haram), I will surely shed your blood." 'Uqbah laughed and said: "O son of Abu Kabshah, how will you get at me outside the Haram?" When the Day of Badr came and 'Uqbah was taken captive, the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered 'Ali, on part of the way, to strike his neck. 'Uqbah said: "O assembly of Quraysh, why should I be the one killed from among you?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "For your denial of Allah and of His Messenger." He said: "And who will care for my little children?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The Fire."

It is related in some reports from the Prophet (ﷺ), and it is said that it is from 'Ali, that he said: "Friends are of four kinds: two believers and two disbelievers. One of the two believers will come forward and it will be said to him: 'What do you say about so-and-so?' meaning his friend. He will say: 'I knew him to enjoin what is good and forbid what is evil. O Allah, give him glad tidings as You gave me glad tidings, and be pleased with him as You were pleased with me.' And one of the two disbelievers will come forward and it will be said to him: 'What do you say about so-and-so?' meaning his friend. He will say: 'I knew him to enjoin what is evil and forbid what is good. O Allah, cause him to enter the Fire as You caused me to enter it, and disgrace him as You disgraced me.'"

In the tafsir, it is said that every brotherhood that exists in this world on the basis of disobedience will turn into enmity on the Day of Resurrection, while every brotherhood based on religion will remain on the Day of Resurrection.

It is related from Mujahid that he said: Ibn 'Abbas said to me: "Love for the sake of Allah, hate for the sake of Allah, be loyal for the sake of Allah, and be hostile for the sake of Allah, for no one attains what is with Allah except by this."

As for His words, ﴿except the righteous﴾, it is said: This refers to the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) when the Messenger of Allah established brotherhood between them. The Messenger of Allah said: "'Ali and I are brothers," and Abu Bakr and 'Umar are brothers, and Talhah and al-Zubayr are brothers, and 'Uthman and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf are brothers, and so on for others besides these.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day﴾. It is narrated that Allah, exalted is He, says on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿O My servants, no fear shall be upon you this Day, nor shall you grieve﴾. Then all creatures raise their heads,

Then He says: ﴿Those who believed in Our signs﴾, and all the believers, Jews and Christians raise their heads. Then He says: ﴿and were Muslims﴾, and all creation lowers their heads except the Muslims. Some of them mentioned His saying: ﴿Those who believed in Our signs and were Muslims﴾ once, in the call.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 70:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, delighted﴾, meaning: you will be made to enjoy bounty. It was also said: you will be honored. In the language, al-hibrah (delight, joy) is gladness and happiness. It is said: there is no delight except that after it comes a tear (ʿibrah). And it is narrated from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir that he said: "Tuhbarun" is listening (to music) in Paradise.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 71:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿There will be passed around them dishes of gold﴾. Al-sihaf (dishes): the large bowls; its singular is ṣaḥfah. It is said in the tafsir: seventy thousand ṣaḥfah, in which are all kinds of food.

His words: ﴿and cups﴾. Al-akwab (cups): its singular is kūb, which is a round vessel that has no handle and no spout.

His words: ﴿And therein is what the souls desire, and delightful to the eyes﴾. That is: what the souls desire. It has been recited thus in some of the well-known recitations.

His words: ﴿and delightful to the eyes﴾. Delight was attributed to the eyes only because beautiful sights delight the souls, so delight was attributed to the eyes, since attributing it to them was more fitting.

His words: ﴿And you therein will abide eternally﴾. That is: you will remain, never to leave.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that is the Paradise which you have been made to inherit, for what you used to do.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: There is not a single person except that he has a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in the Fire. So the believer inherits the dwelling of the disbeliever in Paradise, and the disbeliever inherits the dwelling of the believer in the Fire.

Almost. Translating the passage:

God's words, ﴿For you therein are abundant fruits, from which you eat﴾: the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the criminals will abide in the punishment of Hell, eternally﴾. That is: they will remain (muqimun).

"And His saying: ﴿It shall not be lightened for them﴾, i.e., it shall not be lessened for them.

And His saying: ﴿And they will be in it despairing﴾, i.e., they will be hopeless of coming out. And the mublis (one overwhelmed with despair) in the language is the one who is silent, who falls silent out of bewilderment and despair."
Almighty God's words: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they were themselves the wrongdoers﴾. Its meaning: We requited them for their deeds, and We did not add anything to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 77:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they will call, "O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!"﴾ That is: let your Lord cause us to die. 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: They will call out to [Malik] for forty years. Ibn 'Abbas said: They will call out to him for a thousand years, and then he will answer them, saying: "Indeed you will remain [here]." Then they will call out to Allah, the Exalted, and say: ﴿Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us﴾, but He will not answer them for the length of the life of this world. Then He will say: ﴿Remain in it, and do not speak.﴾ After that, nothing will be heard from them except something like the sound of donkeys, with groaning and sighing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 78:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿We have certainly brought you the truth﴾, i.e., the Qur'an.

And His saying: ﴿But most of you are averse to the truth﴾, i.e., you hated the coming of the truth and the call to it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 79:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Or have they determined a matter?﴾ Al-Ibram (determination) is the firm settling of a matter. Its meaning is that they resolved and agreed upon denial, and We have agreed upon punishment. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿Then indeed, We are determined.﴾ It is also said that ﴿Or have they determined﴾ means: they plotted a plot and schemed a scheme. And His words ﴿Then indeed, We are determined﴾ mean: We counter their plot and scheme with nullification, and We repay them with the recompense of their scheming. This is in the sense of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And they schemed, and Allah schemed, and Allah is the best of schemers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 80:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conferences?﴾ It is related that al-Akhnas and al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth were beside the Ka'bah, and one of them said to his companion: "Do you think Allah hears what we say?" The other said: "If we speak aloud, He hears; and if we speak in secret, He does not hear." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

And His words: ﴿Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ meaning: Yes, He hears. ﴿And Our messengers are with them, recording﴾, i.e., they record what they do and what they say.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 81:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ — the verse is problematic, and there are several opinions concerning it.

The first: the view of Mujahid, which is that its meaning is: Say: If the Most Merciful had a son according to your claim, then I would be the first of the worshippers, meaning that He is a God with no son and no associate, and that what you have said is false and a lie. This is the best of the opinions.

The second opinion: that "in" (إن, "if") here carries the meaning of "ma" (what/not), and its meaning is: Say: the Most Merciful did not have a son, and the statement is complete. Then He said: "then I would be the first of the worshippers." The grammarians consider this unlikely and say: "in" may not be taken to mean "ma" except with great remoteness.

The third opinion: Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers, meaning: the first of those who are disdainful (al-anifin). It is said: "ʿabada" when he is disdainful (anifa). Al-Farazdaq said:

(Those are my fathers, so bring me the like of them... and I disdain that Kulayb be satirized with Darim.)

That is, "anaf" (disdainful). Some have related that ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "It was said to me: You killed ʿUthman, so I disdained and was silent," that is, I was disdainful.

The real meaning of the verse according to this opinion is: I am a jealous one (and He has jealousy), disdainful that a son be attributed to Him as you claim.

The fourth opinion: that this is a negation from both sides, meaning: If the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers, and He has no son, and I am not the first worshipper. This is like a man who says to another: "If you are a scribe, then I am a reckoner," meaning: you are not a scribe and I am not a reckoner. This is related from Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and al-Suddi.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

And His saying: ﴿Lord of the Throne, above what they describe﴾, meaning: above what they ascribe to Him concerning offspring.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So leave them to plunge in vain talk and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.﴾ That is: the Day of Resurrection.

God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾, meaning: worshipped in the heaven and on the earth.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing﴾ has already been explained.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Blessed is He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, meaning: the knowledge of the establishment of the Hour.

And His saying: ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾, meaning: you will be sent back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 86:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And those whom they call upon besides Him have no power of intercession﴾. Mujahid said: that is, Jesus, Uzayr and the angels. Qatadah said: the idols, because the angels and the prophets have intercession.

And His words: ﴿except one who testifies to the truth﴾. Its meaning according to the first view: except for one who testifies to the truth, and that is one who testifies that there is no god but Allah. According to the second view: but one who testifies to the truth, and he intercedes. Based on this, the prophets intercede and the believers intercede.

And His words: ﴿while they know﴾, the meaning is apparent, and its meaning is: they bear witness with knowledge.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah." So how are they turned away?﴾ That is, "how are they diverted?"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 88:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And his saying, "My Lord..."﴾ There are two well-known readings of it: "wa-qīlihi" with a fatḥah on the lām, and "wa-qīlihi" with a kasrah on the lām. A third reading is "qīlahu" with a ḍammah, which is the reading of al-A'raj. As for the fatḥah on the lām, its meaning is: "and He hears his saying," and it refers back to His saying: ﴿Do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private consultations? Yes!﴾ That is: Yes, We hear their secrets and their private consultations, and We hear his saying. Al-Zajjaj said: "and We know his saying," and it refers back to His saying: ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾, and He knows his saying. It is also reported from some of them: "wa-qīlahu" means "and he said," i.e., "qīlahu" means "he said": his statement, regarding the complaint about the disbelievers, meaning the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him.

As for the reading with a kasrah on the lām, its meaning is: "and with Him is the knowledge of his saying," and it is coordinated (ʿaṭf) with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And with Him is the knowledge of the Hour﴾.

As for the ḍammah on the lām, it is on the basis of the inchoative (ibtidāʾ), as though he said: "And his saying, 'My Lord, these are a people who do not believe.'"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 43, verse 89:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿So overlook them﴾: that is, turn away from them. This was before the revelation of the verse of the sword, and it was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of the sword.

And His words, ﴿and say, "Peace"﴾: that is, say that by which you are safe from their evil. Al-Hasan said: "﴿And say, 'Peace'﴾" means: be forbearing toward them. It is also said: this is a peace of farewell (salam tawdi'), and not a peace of greeting (salam tahiyyah).

And His words, ﴿but they will come to know﴾: a threat and a warning.
